title.narrative: Ensuring Inclusiveness and Service Delivery for Persons with Disabilities Project

description.narrative: Often, public support to persons with disabilities (PWDs) focus on providing assistance under the concept of social welfare. However, this project will highlight what PWDs can do to ensure inclusion of PWDs in society, including them in mainstream economic activities, creating opportunities in education and employment, and providing access to the services they need. It will strengthen and institutionalize early identification of disability; improve service delivery and access to the physical environment; improve employment prospects; and contribute to strategic development for PWDs, including social welfare reform, awareness raising, and attitude change.

description.narrative: Access to services and employment for PWDs increased

90% of CWDs enrolled in a portage program receive at least one other service in project areas (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Completed.
The Portage program - an interactive parent-child-facilitator education program for 0-6-year-old children - is one of the services provided by the recently established Development Centers (DC) for PWD in six project aimags. The Mongolian Portage Association agreed to grant MLSP a non-exclusive license to use Portage.
The project consultants developed operational guidelines for the portage early intervention program, including a monitoring and evaluation system. The consultants also developed a training program and training materials for the portage program.
The GADPWD approved the Order А/02 dated 02 January 2024 to collect data to analyze the number of children with disabilities received by the Portage program and other rehabilitation services in project six sites.
In 2024-2025, a total of 16,283 children received services at the DCs in six project aimags. Of these, 3,070 children participated in Portage services, which included home visits by specialists and access to a mobile toy library by the DCs.
The Portage program guidelines were approved by GADPWD order no. A/45 in March 2026. Data Source: MLSP's MIS to be developed in new development and rehabilitation centers, and records from children's disability commissions (annual, once established) Actual value:

Number of employed PWDs increased by 1,500 at least 50% of whom are women (sex disaggregated) (2014 baseline: 24,720) Progress/Status: Being implemented.
Official statistics on the employment of PWDs are derived from the NSO's Labor Force Survey (LFS). However, the employment of PWDs is calculated separately using microdata. So, in some years, employment data for PWDs are not available or only partially reported in survey outputs.
Based on the LFS and related reports from MLSP and ILO, the employment rate of PWDs averaged 25-30% between 2014 and 2018, and since 2019, it has declined to around 18-22%, representing a decrease of 7-10% points. This change is associated with the methodological revision of the LFS in 2019, including the introduction of the Washington Group questions. Therefore, data from 2014-2018 and 2019-2025 are not directly comparable.
According to LFS data, the employment rate of working-age PWDs has shown a declining trend over time. In 2016, approximately 28% (18,000) of working-age PWDs were employed, decreasing to 20% (19,138) in 2020. By 2024, the number of employed PWDs had decreased to 16,175, representing 18% of all working-age PWDs.
For gender, male PWDs consistently account for a higher share of employment. In 2019-2024, 55-58% of employed PWDs were men, while 42-45% were women. As of 2024, 44% (7,175) of employed PWDs are women, compared to 56% (9,000) men. Data Source: Annual NSO labor force survey reports Actual value:

Companies employing at least one PWD by quota increased to 50% (2013 baseline: 29%) Progress/Status: Completed.
The Human Development Research and Training Center (C11) conducted baseline and end-line surveys on the satisfaction of PWD with public services, the compliance with the legal requirement for employment of PWD, inclusive business environment for PWD, accesses to the physical environment, and media audience monitoring on public perception of PWD. The firm collected baseline and endline data in 2020 and 2025, among selected 1000 PWD in 7 aimags and three districts in UB city.
In 20207, the baseline survey results reveal that 76% of companies employ at least one PWD by quota (84.4% in project aimags, and 67.0% in Ulaanbaatar).
In 2025, the end-line survey results reveal that 73% of 200 companies surveyed employ at least one PWD by quota (88.9% in project aimags, and 54.1% in Ulaanbaatar).
49.3% (73) of survey companies employing PWDs reported making some kind of adjustment in workplaces for their employees with disabilities. In project aimags, 52.5% of companies responded that they had taken specific and inclusive measures for PWDs in workplaces, particularly addressing the needs of women with disabilities. In UB, ESC provided 61 employers with workplace adjustment advice and information in 2025. Data Source: Surveys commissioned by the PIU and DPOs (beginning and end of project) Actual value:

PWDs and parents of CWDs satisfied or very satisfied with public services increased to more than 50% (sex disaggregated) (2016 indicative baseline: 40% in Ulaanbaatar) Progress/Status: Completed.
In 2020 , the baseline survey results reveal that PWDs are satisfied with public services in project sites: Ulaanbaatar: 43.3% (46% women) Project 6 sites: 60.5% (66.3% women)
Parents of CWDs satisfied with public services in project sites: Ulaanbaatar: 34 % (46.5% women) Project 6 sites: 61% (56.2% women)
In 2025 , the end-line survey results reveal that PWDs are satisfied with public services in project sites: Ulaanbaatar: 41.6% (48.0% women) Project 6 sites: 58.9% (60.7% women) Overall satisfaction rate: 53.6%
Mothers/female caregivers of CWDs satisfied with public services in project sites: Ulaanbaatar: 58.9 % Project 6 sites: 80.8% sites: 80.8% Overall satisfaction rate: 76.4% Data Source: PIU survey of PWDs in 2021 and 2025 Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 2. Service delivery for PWDs improved Indicator: 12 multidisciplinary teams working with new MLSP standard operating procedures in project areas (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Completed.
In June 2021, the GoM approved Decree №164 to establish the DCs for PWD in six project aimags; in Aug 2022, MLSP approved Order №A/159 on the structure, operational functions, services to be provided at DCs and staff job description. In June 2025, the EA revisited the regulation by issuing Order No. A133. The order provides a more detailed description of the services and operational guidelines, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, orthopedic services, psychology services, social services for adults and children, and a home-based teaching program for CWD.
The project completed construction of DCs in 5 aimags in 2023 and procured assistive devices and essential equipment. Construction of DC in Arkhangai aimag has been completed in December 2025. The MFLSP selected and appointed the management staff for 6 DCs. 6 DCs have been operational since January 2024 (the DC in Arkhangai aimag is operating in a rental premise offered by Arkhangai aimag local government). As of October 2025, 90% of the required staff have been recruited at DCs. Currently, DCs have deployed 12 multidisciplinary teams for adults (in 6 DCs) and children (in 6 DCs), comprising specialists from various disciplines, including medical doctors (MDs), physiotherapists (PTs), occupational therapists (OTs), speech therapists, counselors, psychotherapists, portage instructors, and AT technicians.
The project consultants developed the service delivery design and standard operation procedure (SOP) for services at DCs, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, optometry, primary care, orthopedic services, and portage services. The EA incorporated the consultants' recommendations in MFLSP Minister's Order №А/133 dated 2 June 2025, which regulates the working principles of the multidisciplinary team, the service types, and service delivery guidelines.
The project conducted the following training for multidisciplinary team specialists of DCs in project aimags and other agencies: 1) In 2021-2022, 7 training sessions for 348 potential candidates to work in DCs on the Portage program, social work, physiotherapy and occupational therapy, communication and low vision, and assistive technology. 2) In 2023, 2 training sessions on child physiotherapy and occupational therapy for 50 specialists. 3) In Nov 2023, skills training on assistive technologies for 50 assistive technology specialists. 4) In 2024, 4-days induction training for 50 managers and specialists. 5) In 2024, on-the-job training for 12 assistive technology technicians. The project supported the workshop jointly with NGO "Jaipur Foot" (India) to fit and customize prostheses for 600 PWDs. 6) In May 2025, training on low vision for 12 specialists. 7) In Sep 2025, on-the-job training for Portage service providers to prepare 30 Portage ToTs.
In 2024-2025, the multidisciplinary teams in 6 project aimags, provided services to 21,524 children and 7,255 adults, in accordance with operational and service delivery regulation approved under Order A/133 (2025) of the MFLSP.
PIU developed and submitted a draft methodology and standard operating procedures for delivering early childhood development support and services, which were approved by Order No. A/45 of the Director of the General Authority for Development of PWDs dated March 30, 2026. Data Source: MLSP project reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: Government websites that are made user-friendly for PWD or similar increased by 50% (2016 baseline: none) Progress/Status: Completed.
To ensure access to information for PWD, in 2022, the EA initiated the development of the Mongolian text-to-speech software to improve access to public websites for PWD, especially those with hearing and visual impairments. In 2024, the EA accepted the software and handed it over to the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation, and Communication for incorporation into the government's “E-Mongolia” platform. The Mongolian language text- to-speech software is available as a mobile App and widely used by PWD. Data Source: Reports commissioned by the PIU and DPOs (beginning and end of project) Actual value:

Output: 4. Work and employment for PWDs improved Indicator: Number of PWD job seekers provided skills development and job matching and brokering support by public employment services increased to 400 (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Completed.
In 2022, the project consultants assessed the government policies and services on employment promotion for PWD, and developed (i) model of partnership and cooperation between the employment services run by DPOs and public employment services with the focus of providing job coaching and job brokering services for PWDs, (ii) job profiles and job descriptions for staff in charge of delivering employment services for PWD, (iii) guidelines for job coaching, and brokering services, and (iv) recommendations for improving the monitoring and evaluation.
The project established the Employment Support Center (ESC) for PWD in Ulaanbaatar. Construction of ESC -an eight-floor building attached to the GADPWD - completed in June 2024.
In 2024, the Government approved the Decree №138 on the establishment of the ESC for PWD that will accommodate the provision of employment support services to PWD and employers. By Decree, the ESC will assess the workability of PWD and, based on the assessment, develop individualized case plans covering counselling, vocational training, job placement, coaching, and business incubators for PWD. The ESC will advise employers on adjusting workplaces to the needs of PWD, and facilitate skills training of PWD to meet employers' requirements. Some services at the ESC will be provided by DPOs and financed by the Employment Promotion Fund. The new ESC's operating expenses are included in the social protection minister's portfolio.
The ESC began operations in January 2025. By Government Resolution No. 208 of December 17, 2025, the Vocational Education and Skills Training School (VESTS) for PWDs was transferred to the ESC. Currently, 35 staff work in the ESC for PWD and 15 teachers for VESTS.
The ESC opened the "Job Center" to facilitate job placement for PWD.
In 2025, ESC assessed 300 PWDs workability, and based on assessment, developed individualized case plans, provided counselling, job preparation training, job placement, coaching and offering business incubators for PWDs, in collaboration with contracted 37 DPOs. All participants were involved in job preparation training. 53 PWDs (25 women) were placed in jobs with 45 companies. DPOs provided 61 employers with workplace adjustment advice and information.
DCs in 6 project aimags provided job counseling and mediation services to 957 PWDs; of these, 122 (67 women) were placed in jobs, in collaboration with 75 DPOs, between 2024 and 2025.
As of 2025, in total, ESC and 6 DCs provided 1,257 PWD job seekers with job counseling, training, job brokering and business incubation support. Data Source: MLSP's MIS in public employment services (annual) Actual value:

Output: 4. Work and employment for PWDs improved Indicator: Number of PWDs supported by DPOs using new employment service approaches increased to 300, at least 120 of whom are women (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Completed.
In February 2025, Employment Support Center for PWD is operationalized.
The ESC selected 37 DPOs and contracted to deliver welfare employment services, job brokering in open jobs and business incubation services with financial support from the Employment Promotion Fund in 2025.
The methodology for assessing the employability skills of PWDs based on the ICF by four types of disabilities (vision, hearing, movement, and intellectual) was approved by Order A/38 of the Director of the ESC dated September 10, 2025. A methodological training on using the assessment methodology in their activities was organized on August 29, 2025, involving 23 persons from the DPOs and 6 employment staff from the ESC.
Training on preparing a personal plan based on employability assessment, to provide employability skills tailored to PWDs' skills and interests, was organized in October 2025, involving representatives of 28 DPOs providing integrated services for PWDs. In 2025, 37 DPOs provided new employment services to 300 PWDs, of whom 144 were women. Data Source: MLSP's new MIS module developed for contracting DPOs (annual) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Access to social welfare benefits for PWDs simplified and amount of benefit linked to the three levels of support needs of PWDs by the end of the project increased by 60% (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Being Implemented.
In 2022, the project consultants reviewed the existing social welfare system in Mongolia and international practices on disability allowances, caregivers' benefits, and community-based social welfare services. They provided recommendations for legislative changes to improve targeting and financial support for PWD.
Since 2020, the Government has increased caregiver allowances three times in alignment with the 3 levels of support needs of PWDs: 1. Caregiver allowance (MNT 84,500 in 2018) was increased to MNT 123,000 under Resolution No.25 in 2020, to MNT 275,000 under Resolution No.237 in 2023, and to MNT 302,500 under Resolution No. 122 in 2024. The number of beneficiaries has steadily risen, from 65,191 caregivers in 2021 to 77,844 in 2024. Of those in 2024, 17,166 were caring for PWDs requiring permanent care, and 15,064 were caregivers of CWDs. 2. Cash support benefits (different amounts depending on target groups) was increased to MNT 188,000 under Resolution No.25 in 2020, to MNT 288,000 under Resolution No.237 in 2023, to MNT 375,000 under Resolution No. 122 in 2024. In 2024, 70,861 PWDs and CWDs received cash support benefits. This included monthly assistance - equivalent to the social welfare pension - for 15,178 CWDs under 16 requiring permanent care, and quarterly assistance for 55,683 PWDs aged 16 and above in need of permanent care. 3. Social welfare pension for PWDs aged 16 and above with 50% or higher loss of working capacity (MNT 188,000 in 2018) was increased to MNT 288,000 under Resolution No.25 in 2020, to MNT 325,000 under Resolution No.237 in 2023, to MNT 375,000 Resolution N.122 in 2024. In 2024, 36.623 PWDs received social welfare pension.
Access to caregiver allowance, social welfare pension, and cash support benefits was simplified through the introduction of online applications, processing, and decisions on public sector websites. Data Source: MLSP's new regulations prepared and approved (ad hoc) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Every child assessed by the medical commissions in project areas has an ICF diagnosis completed (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Being implemented.
The ESC conducted a two-stage survey of working-age PWD interested in job placement. As of 2025, 49000 PWD have been enrolled in the 1st-stage study, of whom 13400 are interested in job-coaching services.
In the second stage study, ESC conducted an assessment of the workability of 10,076 PWDs interested in job-placing services, using the ICF simplified tools prepared by the project consultants.
Data were collected using assessment tools covering physical activity, structure, involvement, and personal and environmental factors, and were subsequently classified into 4 basic work ability patterns.
4,229 PWDs (42%) fall under pattern 3, who have the capacity to work. A further 38% are classified under pattern 2a and 2b, who need some mental and physical support in order to be employed, while 2023 (20%) fall under pattern 1 or those with limited ability to work and a high need for welfare services.
The findings of this study provide a strong database for the specific needs and work capacities of PWDs, thereby improving the effectiveness of services. Data Source: General Authority for Social Insurance and MLSP internal reports and project documentation (annual) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Media content on disability rights and issues reaching target audiences and meeting quality criteria set by DPOs increased by 40% (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Completed.
In 2020, the project consultant developed a communication strategy for public awareness raising and attitude change towards PWD.
The MFLSP approved communication strategy in 2020, overseen by a Media Steering Group comprising representatives from DPOs, MFLSP, and media experts.
In 2021-2022, seven DPOs were contracted to develop public awareness contents, which were broadcasted through public events, national TV, radio programs, and social media advertisements. The contents are used by DCs to improve public awareness and attitude towards PWD.
The project conducted a media monitoring survey on awareness-raising activities 3 times in Dec 2021, July 2022, and Sep 2022. Out of 200 PWDs who participated in the survey, 71.4 percent were satisfied with the published articles' visual presentation and the content.
In 2020-2025, a nation-wide communication campaign was implemented to raise awareness on disability rights and issues, including access to education for CWDs and to address violence against women and girls with disabilities, through multi-channels, including TV, radio, newspapers, and online platforms. Targeted content reached more than 5,300 PWDs, of whom 2,900 (54%) were women. Complementary public awareness activities, implemented in collaboration with NGOs and diverse stakeholders, reached an additional 3,121 PWDs, including 1,700 women (54.5%).
The PIU prepared draft Guidelines for public communication activities to be used by DCs and submitted to the MFLSP in August 2025. The Guidelines for communication activities to promote public awareness of the rights of PWDs were approved by Order No. A/229 of the Minister of Family, Labor and Social Protection, dated December 5, 2025.
In 2025, the project also organized key training and awareness events to promote employment for PWDs, as part of the “2025 Promoting Employment for PWDs.” In May 2025, the MFLSP and PIU jointly organized capacity-building and awareness-raising activities in Dundgovi and Khuvsgul aimags. In addition, the Arkhangai aimag DC, in collaboration with the General Authority for the Development of PWDs, organized the Mongolia Occupational Therapy International Forum III. Data Source: PIU media monitoring and audience research (annual) Actual value:

Output: 2. Service delivery for PWDs improved Indicator: Eight PWD development and rehabilitation centers according to universal design specifications built or constructed (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Being implemented.
In April 2020, MLSP recruited a design firm, which prepared schematic design of DCs following the universal design requirements and detailed engineering design (approved by the CDC in 2021).
Construction of DCs for PWD in six project aimags commenced in June 2021. In March 2023, the construction was completed and commissioned in 5 aimags (Darkhan-uul, Dornod, Dundgovi, Khovd, and Khuvsgul).
Project procured assistive technology and medical equipment (1224 pieces of 112 types) (G1-Lot 1); office furniture (1026 pieces) (G1-Lot 3); IT equipment (246 pieces of 19 types) (G1-Lot 2); mobile toy library and child-parent training aids (3402 pieces of 245 types) (G1-Lot 4) which were delivered and installed in DCs in 2023.
Construction of the DC in Arkhangai aimag has been delayed. The contractor and the EA had disagreements over the contractor's poor performance, which continued for 2 years. In October 2024, the EA established a dispute resolution committee to resolve this issue and reached an agreement to continue with the same contractor. The construction work resumed in March 2025 and completed in December 2025. On February 12, 2026, the State Expertise commissioned the construction works and accepted with minor recommendations that the contractor is addressing.
The project is establishing two additional DCs in Zavkhan aimag and the Bayanzurkh district of Ulaanbaatar city, based on ADB's April 2024 memo on minor changes. In April 2025, the EA initiated bidding for the DC constructions in Zavkhan aimag and in July 2025, for Bayanzurkh district. In October 2025, the EA awarded the contract for the Zavkhan aimag DC to Morinsuvd LLC and the contract for the Bayanzurkh district DC to Khukh Khairkhan LLC.
The schedule of construction work for the DCs in Zavkhan aimag and Bayanzurkh district has been prepared in collaboration with the contractors; construction works commenced in April 2026.
The external infrastructure drawings and budget of the DC in Bayanzurkh district were approved by verification on January 20, 2026. The IFB was posted on 25 March 2026 with a bid submission deadline of 28 April 2026 to be followed by the bid evaluation. The contract award is expected within April 2026. Data Source: MLSP project reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: PWDs who receive assistive devices in project areas increased to 15% for both men and women (sex disaggregated) (2016 indicative baseline: 6%) Progress/Status: Completed.
In 2020, the baseline survey on PWD satisfaction with public services revealed that out of 1,000 respondents, 346 people, or 34.6% (155 or 44.6% were women), are satisfied with the quality and comfort of assistive devices, including wheelchairs, hearing aids, and prostheses.
In 2021, project consultants developed a draft strategy on assistive technology in Mongolia.
In 2022, the project upgraded the Prosthetic Factory of the GADPWD by building a new ventilation system and procuring new orthopedic manufacturing equipment and spare parts for the existing machinery (201 pieces of 61 types of equipment). With this investment, the Prosthesis factory's capacity increased. The factory provides services to over 2,300 PWD annually with 10 types of prosthetic and 16 types of orthopedic products. Of these, 580 (25%) PWDs' products were tailored and manufactured based on specific needs of PWDs, and over 550 (24%) PWDs were provided with ready-to-use manufactured products. The factory also provided consultations to 1,070 (46%) PWDs and the mobile outreach services to 115 (5%) PWDs.
In 2023, to increase AT technicians, the project upgraded the capacity of the Vocational Training Center under GADPWD by procuring the required equipment for training courses (430 pieces of 72 types. In 2025, Vocational Training Center trained 22 assistive technology technicians recruited in DCs in project sites, in the Prosthesis Factory, and the Development Center for CWD in Ulaanbaatar.
The project established DCs for PWD in 6 aimags with prosthesis units to manufacture and repair prostheses for those in need.
According to the end-line survey, 31.6% of PWDS and 30% of women with disabilities in the project aimags are using orthopedic and assistive devices. Of these, 43% were provided by the social welfare fund.
The PWDs who received assistive devices in the project aimags have increased to 19.8 percent: 20.4% for women and 19.0% for men. For satisfaction with the assistive devices: (i) 44.5% of the surveyed PWDs and 42% of women were satisfied with the quality of use; (ii) 45.7 percent of PWDs and 53.4% of women, considered the assistive devices to be comfortable; (iii) 50.8% of female PWDs considered that assistive devices were adjusted to their needs.
As reported, DCs for PWDs in 6 aimags provided services to 11,839 PWDs in 2024-2025, while 1,000 PWDs and 468 women with disabilities received assistive devices.
PIU prepared and submitted a draft Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for Assistive Technology Services to the MFLSP, with an official letter No. 26/15 dated February 26, 2026.
In 2025, by Government Resolution No. 207 dated December 17, 2025, the Prosthetic Factory was re-organized as the National Center for Rehabilitation and Assistive Technology. The main functions of the National Center are to provide rehabilitation health services to PWDs; manufacture and supply prosthetic, orthotic, and assistive technology products; improve the accessibility of services; provide methodological guidance, training, and capacity-building for staff, officials, and professionals working with PWDs; and deliver services aimed at enhancing the equal participation of PWDs in society. Output: 1. Early identification of CWDs strengthened and institutionalized Indicator: Early identification model of CWDs in MLSP initiated and implemented (2016 baseline: not initiated) Progress/Status: Completed.
In 2021, project consultants assessed the current situation of the early identification system in Mongolia, studied international experiences on the early screening for children, and developed the Mongolian Rapid Baby Scale for infant development (MORBAS) for 9, 18, and 36 months old children. MORBAS is incorporated in the Child Health and Development Book (Pink Book) and approved by MOH Order №A/347 dated 29 Sep 2023.
In 2025, the project trained 1254 health personnel and family doctors working at the primary level on the usage of the modified Pink Book.
The project consultants assisted MOH to modify Doctor Baumann's developmental delay assessment tool for the referral level hospitals by reflecting the Mongolian context. Consultants also edited the video training (50 hours), adding Mongolian subtitles for medical personnel.
In 2023-2024, the project conducted online training for tertiary level referral hospital doctors on using Baumann's developmental delay assessment tool. The online training was attended by medical doctors from the National Center for Maternal and Child Health, the Rehabilitation Center for CWD, and aimag general hospitals in project aimags.
In September 2024, Doctor Baumann's team conducted 4 days of face-to-face training with 43 participants from project aimags as well as the National Center for Maternal and Child Health, the Rehabilitation Center for CWD, the Children's Central Sanatorium, and the Second Center for Maternal and Child Health.
The project procured necessary devices for assessment of children's development delays, like a device to assess hearing disparities (Sentiero Desktop Diagnostic grade), vision screening (Plusoptix), and other testing tools, and distributed them to project aimags and tertiary level hospitals.
Consultant C2 assisted improving functions of the multisectoral commissions responsible for the disability assessment of children, provided recommendations on the commission structure, tasks, and job description for commission members and developed operational guidelines and procedures and M&E. Based on recommendations, in 2021, the MLSP, MES, and MOH jointly approved a decree (A/220, A/475, A/812 of 30 December 2021) to endorse revised guidelines and methodology for the development assessment and assistance for CWD to be used by multisectoral commissions. In 2022, the project trained members of the multisectoral commission and sub-commission in project aimags and Ulaanbaatar on newly approved guidelines and methodology.
In 2024-2025, 3,057 CWDs attended early screening at DCs in 6 project aimags. Of these, 1,132 CWDs assessed by the Health, Education and Social Protection Commission for CWDs. In June 2021, MLSP established the Social Protection Call Center at the ministry, which has specific modules for communicating and providing information for PWD, including those with hearing impairment. The project supported purchasing a three-year subscription fee in connection to the state inter-sectoral web platform www.duudlaga.mn.
As of October 2023, the Call center responded to around 80,000 calls, through hotline number 1800-0724. Over 80% of callers were asked to social welfare, insurance related questions and clarifications.
In 2025, the Call center moved to the Employment Support Center for PWDs. In 2025, the Call center responded to 724 calls and served 6,824 persons with disabilities who attended the ESC in person. Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: Standards for accessibility harmonized with health and safety standards and made widely available to decision makers (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Being implemented.
In 2021, the project consultants reviewed the situation with the accessibility audit; prepared a report with findings from a comparison of 2015, 2020, and 2022 accessibility audit conducted by Universal Development NGO; developed tools for conducting the accessibility audit with the support of DPOs; and, based on the review of current legislation and standards on accessibility to construction, transport, and information for PWD, developed proposals to improve legislation and standards on the accessibility of construction, transportation, and information.
By Order No. A/190 of the MFLSP of 2022 established a working group to conduct an accessibility assessment in Ulaanbaatar for each type of disability. Accordingly, by Order No. A/230 of the Minister of Construction and Urban Development of 2022 established a sub-working group to assess compliance of government buildings in Ulaanbaatar, and to make recommendations on improving accessibility.
The sub-working group prepared an assessment checklist with 53 criteria based on relevant construction norms and standards (BNBD 31-23-22). A total of 23 government organizations, including 16 ministries and 6 Governance Administration Offices in Ulaanbaatar was assessed in 2022. The assessment report was submitted to the Ministry of Construction and Urban Development, and the recommendations were presented to relevant organizations.
The project consultants assisted the EA in developing a new Bill on Barrier-free and Accessibility. The EA is conducting consultations with government agencies and DPOs. Project consultants also assisted in preparing the costing of implementation of the Bill required for submission to the parliament.
The working group at the EA finalized the concept, needs assessment and cost estimates of a draft law on Accessibility and amendments to 20 accompanying laws. Currently, the draft law on accessibility is being discussed by the Government.
The Minister of Family, Labor, and Social Protection and the Minister of Justice and Internal Affairs jointly approved the concept of the draft law on Mongolian Sign Language on December 9, 2025.
